key_insight: AP-OOD uses attention-weighted pooling over token embeddings to produce a single, more informative OOD score, capturing token-level signals that simple averaging misses.
problem_solved: How to aggregate token-level representations from language models into a robust scalar OOD score—average pooling dilutes informative tokens and hurts detection; AP-OOD addresses this with a token-aware, semi-supervised pooling strategy.
method: Compute token embeddings from a pre-trained language model and learn attention weights that emphasize OOD-relevant tokens.
Pool token embeddings via the learned attention to obtain a compact representation and derive a scalar OOD score from it.
Train attention and scoring components in a semi-supervised setup that leverages labeled in-distribution data plus unlabeled or proxy OOD signals to shape attention.
impact: Provides NLP practitioners a simple, plug-in method to improve OOD detection reliability by leveraging token-level cues—leading to better uncertainty estimation and safer model deployment.
visual_elements: Schematic: tokens → embeddings → attention weights (heatmap) → attention-pooled vector → scalar OOD score
Side-by-side bar/line chart: AP-OOD vs. average pooling on standard OOD metrics (e.g., AUROC / FPR95) to show performance gain
Example text with attention overlay highlighting tokens driving the OOD decision (attention heatmap on words)
Training-flow diagram showing semi-supervised signals: labeled ID data + unlabeled/proxy OOD data → attention learning → scoring head
paper_title: AP-OOD: Attention Pooling for Out-of-Distribution Detection
paper_authors: Claus Hofmann, Christian Huber, Bernhard Lehner, Daniel Klotz, Sepp Hochreiter
